gloss: all things; all creation; everything in existence

definitions.gloss: all things; all creation; everything in existence
definitions.explanation: All things in the universe or in nature. A literary and philosophical term referring to the entirety of creation.

examples.japanese: {万物|ばんぶつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{霊長|れいちょう}⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧⟦{人間|にんげん}→人間：03523_ningen⟧。
examples.english: Humans, the supreme beings of all creation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{万物|ばんぶつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{息|いき}を{吹|ふ}き{返|かえ}す→息を吹き返す：18889_ikiwofukikaesu⟧。
examples.english: When spring arrives, all things come back to life.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古代|こだい}→古代：05324_kodai⟧⟦ギリシャ→ギリシャ：28897_girisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{哲学者|てつがくしゃ}→哲学者：23941_tetsugakusha⟧タレス⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{万物|ばんぶつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{根源|こんげん}→根源：19932_kongen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{説|と}いた→説く：14245_toku⟧。
examples.english: The ancient Greek philosopher Thales taught that the origin of all things is water.

notes:
A literary and philosophical term meaning "all things in creation." Composed of {万|ばん} (ten thousand/myriad) + ⟦{物|ぶつ}→〜物：28336_butsu⟧ (things). Used in elevated, poetic, or philosophical contexts rather than everyday speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {万物|ばんぶつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{霊長|れいちょう}: the lord of all creation (i.e., humankind)
- {万物|ばんぶつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{根源|こんげん}→根源：19932_kongen⟧: the origin of all things
- {万物|ばんぶつ}⟦{流転|るてん}→流転：22107_ruten⟧: all things are in flux (a Buddhist and philosophical concept)
- {万物|ばんぶつ}⟦{生|い}き→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧し⟦{生|い}け→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧るもの: all living things

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{森羅万象|しんらばんしょう}→森羅万象：06149_shinrabanshou⟧: all things in nature; the whole universe — a more elaborate four-character idiom
- すべて⟦の→の：09472_no⟧もの: everything — the plain everyday expression
- {万象|ばんしょう}: all phenomena — similar literary register

USAGE:
The famous phrase {万物|ばんぶつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{霊長|れいちょう} (literally "the most excellent spirit among all creation") is the traditional Japanese expression for "humanity as the supreme being in nature."
